methods.label: Track the positions under rotation
methods.explanation:
At any position, the final color is black if either the original square there was black or the square rotated into that position was black. A position remains white exactly when both of those original squares were white.

A quarter-turn fixes the center, cycles the four corners among themselves, and cycles the four edge-middle squares among themselves. The center must initially be black. In either four-position cycle, call positions consecutive when one rotates into the other. The condition is that no two consecutive positions, including the last and first, may both initially be white.

Count the valid patterns in one such cycle by their number of white squares:

With no white squares, there is \(1\) pattern.

With one white square, there are \(4\) choices for its position.

With two white squares, they must be opposite in the cycle, giving \(2\) choices.

Three or four white squares cannot work, since they necessarily include consecutive whites. These cases are disjoint and cover every valid pattern, so each cycle has
\[
1+4+2=7
\]
valid patterns.

The center, corner cycle, and edge-middle cycle use disjoint positions, so their choices combine in \(1\cdot7\cdot7=49\) ways. Each resulting coloring is counted once by its restrictions to these three groups. All \(2^9=512\) initial colorings are equally likely by the independent fair color choices. Therefore the probability is \(\boxed{\frac{49}{512}}\), choice A.
